thread:
Alex: quick check — we need to decide whether to switch the runtime from per-request continuous penalty scores to a compact 4-bin penalty scheme for region/tier weighting. thinking: much cheaper memory + faster scoring but risks losing fine-grained fairness.
Maria: +1 on trying a compact scheme in sim first. operationally the memory wins are real for the edge.
Priya: is the primary goal cost predictability or latency tail smoothing? those are different targets.
Alex: both, but prioritize predictability for now. we can accept a small latency delta if p95 stays within SLO.
Jason: can we make bins adaptive? e.g., cluster distribution of latencies and then pick bin thresholds per-tenant?
Priya: adaptive thresholds add complexity to rollout and explainability. I worry about metric drift making buckets unstable.
Maria: simulation idea: run 14-day traffic replay with current continuous scores vs 4-bin static vs 4-bin adaptive. collect p50/p95/p99, cost-per-token, and per-tenant fairness delta.
policy-sim-bot: scheduled sim job queued: sim-run/1719140073-compact-bins. expect ~3h runtime with our current cluster.
Alex: config sketch for the static 4-bin (proposal):
```
penalty_scheme: compact_v1
bins: [0.0, 0.25, 0.6, 1.0] # normalized penalty thresholds
weights_by_bin: [1.0, 0.8, 0.5, 0.2]
apply_to: [region_penalty, tier_penalty]
max_delta_per_request: 0.15
```
Priya: question: what does `max_delta_per_request` mean here? to cap the effect of bucketization?
Alex: yes — prevents single-request score jumps > 0.15 relative to continuous score. safety knob for rollout.
Jason: we'll need telemetry hooks: emit `score_before`, `score_after`, `bin_id`, and `tenant_id_hash` for aggregation. also histogram of delta.
Maria: note on rollout: start with shadowing + daily canary to 1% then 10% then 50% if sims look good. ops-runbook should include rollback if p99 latency increases > 10% or per-tenant regret > 5%.
Priya: ops note — we must ensure policy audit logs still allow forensic replay. compact bins mean we lose resolution; log both raw continuous and bin id for at least 30 days.
Alex: agree, raw continuous for replay retained for 30d then drop to bin-only to save storage. add a migration flag: `emit_raw_score: boolean`. default true for canary.
policy-sim-bot: sim job started: sim-run/1719140073-compact-bins at 2024-04-24T16:12:00Z (eta ~3h). results will be posted back to this thread.
Jason: one more tradeoff: bucketization interacts with caching/batching heuristics — small score changes can flip routing and break cache locality. include `cache_affinity_penalty` in telemetry to measure.
Maria: if cache churn spikes, prefer bias toward higher affinity (we can add a multiplier to reduce bin effect when cache_affinity > threshold).
Priya: doc update needed in policy-engine/README: new compact_v1 scheme, rollout steps, telemetry schema. I'll draft a short RFC follow-up and add migration checklist.
Alex: cool — next actions: 1) run sims (policy-sim-bot), 2) Priya to draft RFC follow-up, 3) Jason to add telemetry and canary metrics, 4) Maria to own ops runbook and rollback criteria. I'll coordinate canary windows.
Maria: tagging @oncall in ops channel when we flip to 1% canary.
Priya: ping me when sim results are in — I'll include sample graphs in the RFC.
Alex: thanks all. trying to keep the initial experiment conservative — compact bins + max_delta cap + raw-score logging for replay.
policy-sim-bot: sim-run/1719140073-compact-bins completed. summary: p95 change +1.8%, cost -6.4%, per-tenant-regret median 0.6%. full artifacts: s3://redwood-sims/1719140073/ (uploading).
Maria: nice — baseline looks promising. Priya, can you start the RFC draft? include suggested thresholds for rollback based on sim.
Priya: will do, aiming for draft by EOD tomorrow.
Alex: great — if sim artifacts look okay we'll start 1% shadow->canary next week.
Jason: adding telemetry PR now. will link PR here when ready.
Maria: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
